title: Professional guitarist with ten years of right-arm dystonia that has spread beyond playing

provenance.citation: Adapted from a published, openly licensed case report (article CC BY 4.0; videos CC0 1.0) with patient consent for publication obtained by the original authors. Full citation is held in the reference file because the article title names the diagnosis. Fields the source does not report are marked as such and were not invented.

demographics.occupation: Professional guitarist (stopped performing about five years after symptom onset)

chief_complaint: Referred for reassessment of right upper limb dystonia of about ten years' duration, previously diagnosed as guitarist's cramp.
history_of_present_illness: At age 27 he began practicing guitar for most of his waking hours. About three months later he developed difficulty holding the pick, with excessive extension of the right wrist and intermittent tremulous movements of the right fingers while playing. At 29 he was diagnosed with guitarist's cramp and treated with clonazepam and trihexyphenidyl without benefit. Switching from guitar to piano temporarily abolished the abnormal movements, but they returned. Over the following years the problem stopped being confined to playing: it is now also triggered by everyday tasks with the right hand, such as opening and closing screw-cap bottles and brushing his teeth. About five years after onset he had so much difficulty playing that he stopped performing. He is now referred, at 37, for reassessment.

symptom_timeline.event: Intensive guitar practice; ~3 months later, difficulty holding the pick with excessive right wrist extension and intermittent tremulous finger movements
Diagnosed with guitarist's cramp; clonazepam and trihexyphenidyl ineffective
Switching to piano transiently abolished the movements; they later recurred
Loss of task specificity: dystonia also with opening screw-cap bottles and toothbrushing
Stopped performing because of difficulty playing
Referred for reassessment of upper limb dystonia

movement_findings.observation: Opening a screw-cap bottle with the right hand provokes dystonic posturing of the right upper limb with excessive wrist extension and finger hyperextension (source Video S1).
Dystonic posturing is action-induced, appearing mainly during skilled voluntary movements of the right arm; not present at rest.
No parkinsonism, pyramidal signs, or cerebellar ataxia.

neurological_exam.reflexes: No pyramidal signs (individual reflex grades not reported in source)
neurological_exam.gait: Not specifically described in source; no lower-limb involvement reported
neurological_exam.other: Sensory and autonomic examinations unremarkable. Action-induced right upper limb dystonia as in mf_01–mf_02.

labs.test: Electrolytes, renal function, CBC, liver function, urinalysis

labs.note: Value not reported in source. Slit-lamp examination and 24-hour urine copper not reported.

family_history: No family history of neurological disorders reported.
social_history: Not reported in source, beyond occupation and intensive practice at onset. No regular medication before symptom onset.
prior_workup_and_opinions: Age 29: diagnosed with guitarist's cramp (task-specific focal dystonia); treated with clonazepam and trihexyphenidyl without benefit. No other prior opinions reported.
